title: Reaching the Francophone Community in Ghana

ms.promise:

ms.report:
On 23rd November 2023, a seminar was organised for members of the Francophone community at the Alliance Francaise School in Accra. A total of 51 participants were present and were taken through presentations on 'The Fundamentals of Blockchain' which also discussed the Cardano blockchain in particular. Other presentations were on 'Project Catalys and Opportunities' and also on the 'Emurgo Yoroi Wallet'. Participants were guided to register on Ideascale and those who were interested in becoming reviewers were also guided to complete the reviewer registration form. 
Participants were also supported to download and create their own Yoroi wallets. Five ada was given to each person who created a wallet to enable them stake their ada for eventual rewards. A total of 31 people created wallets. At the end of the seminar, certificates of participation were given to participants as a way of encouraging them in the learning process toknow more about the Cardano blockchain, Project Catalyst and the Cardano community in general.
The monthly report submitted to the Catalyst Team on 5th December 2023, which is the report I referred to in the milestone, provided the number of participants for whom wallets were created as 31. I was informed by Catalyst Team member, Danny Ribar, that the names were not relevant, which is why they were not included in the report. The report in question is therefore the monthly report which has been already sent. Kindly let me know if there is any other report I am required to sent to the Catalyst team as a funded proposer and I will gladly oblige.
Link to video and pictures: https://youtu.be/0DF0U1eUvCQ

ms.report:
On 29th November 2023, a 2nd seminar was organised for members of the Francophone community at the University of Media Arts and Communication (UNIMac)- Ghana Institute of Languages in Accra. A total of 72 participants were present and were taken through presentations on 'The Fundamentals of Blockchain' which also discussed the Cardano blockchain in particular. Other presentations were on 'Project Catalyst and Opportunities' and also on the 'Emurgo Yoroi Wallet'. Participants were guided to register on Ideascale and those who were interested in becoming reviewers were also guided to complete the reviewer registration form since the registration window was open at the time.
Participants were also supported to download and create their own Yoroi wallets. Five ada was credited to the wallet of each person who created a wallet to enable them stake their ada for eventual rewards. A total of 43 people created wallets. A WhatsApp group has been created for all participants who were present at this seminar, to ensure regular engagements with them and guide them through any challenges they may have in their interaction on Ideascale and Project Catalyst. They will eventually join the Africa Townhall mailing list so they can fully participate in Africa related Cardano events and meetings. The link to a short video and pictures of the event and to the seminar documents is below.
Link to video and pictures: https://youtu.be/C9AnOcX7EHg
Link to seminar documents: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/138Q7mS9RT3T12xyjRgwJk0E2vwpGbtxL?usp=drive_link

ms.report:
On 23rd February 2024, the 3rd seminar was organised for francophone students of the Perez University College. A total of 25 participants were present and were taken through the three main presentations. Eight (8) joined the Cardano community and have expressed the desire to become reviewers in the next funding cycle. The number of participants fell short of the estimated 65 because the major educational institutions we targeted, which have large francophone student populations were unwilling to allow us hold the seminars in their institutions. The school authorities expressed misgivings about the kind of information we would be sharing with the students as a result of the wrong perception of cryptocurrency being a scam. We were therefore left with the option of contacting smaller and relatively new institutions with lower student populations. Perez University College is one such institution. 
A WhatsApp group has been created for all participants who were present at this seminar, to ensure regular engagement with them and guide them through any challenges they may have in their interaction on Ideascale and Project Catalyst.
A possible collaboration is being discussed to train Cardano developers at the Perez University College. The Information Technology Department will assess its capacity to introduce courses related to Cardano and determine how they will be rolled out. If this collaboration can be done, a proposal will be submitted to Project Catalyst for funding to implement it.
Link to video and pictures of the 3rd seminar: https://youtu.be/uHaGH_MNtuk
A close out report and video have been prepared as the key requirement for project completion. The Google drive link to the close out report is: https://drive.google.com/file/d/17i1hv5AUEilXINNYWtYGJDoRULpon7NW/view?usp=sharing
The link to the close out video is: https://youtu.be/RHSYIxDZXJ0
